summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder managed with a chronic Foley catheter, was admitted for generalized weakness and fatigue consistent with recurrent urinary tract infections. He had recently run out of methenamine, a prophylactic medication, and presented with symptoms suggestive of UTI, including diarrhea. He was treated with IV vancomycin and cefepime initially, then transitioned to oral sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (Bactrim) after urine culture identified Escherichia coli sensitive to Bactrim. His symptoms resolved during the hospital stay, and diarrhea improved with no infectious cause found. He was discharged home with home health services to assist with Foley catheter changes, continuing methenamine for prophylaxis and completing a 14-day course of Bactrim.
